title: .ai
summary:
.ai is the Internet country code top-level domain (ccTLD) for Anguilla, a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is administered by the government of Anguilla. It is a popular domain hack with companies and projects related to the artificial intelligence industry.

A .ai domain can be suspended or revoked if the domain is involved in illegal activity such as violating trademarks or copyrights, and usage must not violate the laws of Anguilla. On 16 December 2017, the .ai registry started supporting the Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP) and migrated all of its domains onto an EPP system, allowing many registrars to sell .ai domains.

The registration fees earned from .ai domains go to the treasury of the Government of Anguilla. As per a 2018 New York Times report, the total revenue generated from selling .ai domains was $2.9 million. In 2023, Anguillas government made about US$32 million from fees collected for registering .ai domains, amounting to over 10 percent of gross domestic product for the territory.

Domain costs depend on the registrar, with yearly fees ranging from US$140 (the base fee established by Anguilla) to $200. Though such trends are primarily seen among new AI-based companies or startups, many established AI and tech companies preferred not to opt for .ai domains. For example, DeepMind retained its .com domain, and Meta redirected its facebook.ai domain to ai.meta.com.
